extracted.intended_audience: general readers and video game industry stakeholders (publishers, retailers, parents)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards used by the Entertainment Software Rating Board (ESRB) to classify and label video games and related marketing/digital products in North America. Covers rating categories, content descriptors, interactive-element labels, rating submission processes, enforcement, and marketing/privacy rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rating Pending (RP)
rubrics_metrics.description: This symbol is used in promotional materials for games which have not yet been assigned a final rating by the ESRB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Displayed in promotional materials prior to final rating assignment; intended to signal that a rating will be provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rating Pending – Likely Mature (RP Likely Mature)
rubrics_metrics.description: Used in promotional materials for games which have not yet been assigned a final rating by the ESRB, but are anticipated to carry a 'Mature' rating based on their content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates expectation of a Mature rating prior to formal review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Everyone (E)
rubrics_metrics.description: Games with this rating contain content that the ESRB believes is suitable for all ages, including minimal cartoon, fantasy, or mild violence, and infrequent use of profane language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior to 2018, ESRB suggested ages 6+ for E; icons displayed on packaging and promotional materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Everyone 10+ (E10+)
rubrics_metrics.description: Games with this rating contain content that the ESRB believes is suitable for ages 10 and over, including a larger amount of cartoon, fantasy, or mild violence than 'E', mild use of profane language, and minimal suggestive themes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduced in 2005 to designate content between E and T.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teen (T)
rubrics_metrics.description: Games with this rating contain content that the ESRB believes is suitable for ages 13 and over, including aggressive depictions of violence with minimal blood, moderate suggestive themes, crude humor, and stronger use of profane language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used when content exceeds E10+ but is not intense enough for Mature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mature 17+ (M)
rubrics_metrics.description: Games with this rating contain content that the ESRB believes is suitable for ages 17 and over, including intense and/or realistic depictions of violence, blood and gore, sexual content, and frequent use of profane and vulgar language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most restrictive mainstream consumer rating; retailers commonly enforce with ID checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adults Only 18+ (AO)
rubrics_metrics.description: Games with this rating contain content that the ESRB believes is suitable for ages 18 and over only; the majority of AO-rated titles are adult video games with graphic or explicit sexual content. AO has also been assigned for extreme violence or gambling with real money in some cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Console manufacturers and many retailers will refuse to license or stock AO-rated titles, severely limiting commercial distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early Childhood (EC) (retired)
rubrics_metrics.description: This rating denoted content aimed towards a preschool audience; games with the rating do not contain content parents would find objectionable. The EC rating was retired in 2018 due to underuse; such content today would receive an E rating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical/retired category; no longer assigned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content descriptors (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: ESRB ratings incorporate one or more of 32 'content descriptors' to provide detailed information about specific types and levels of objectionable content in a game (violence, language, sexual content, nudity, alcohol/tobacco/drugs, crude/mature humor, gambling, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Descriptors appear on the full label (typically on back packaging). When a descriptor is preceded by 'Mild' it conveys low frequency/intensity unless otherwise defined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alcohol Reference
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference to alcohol in any form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animated Blood
rubrics_metrics.description: Content includes unrealistic and/or discolored blood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blood
rubrics_metrics.description: Graphics include realistic blood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blood and Gore
rubrics_metrics.description: Graphics include realistic blood and the mutilation of body parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cartoon Violence
rubrics_metrics.description: Violent actions that look cartoon-like in nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comic Mischief
rubrics_metrics.description: Content includes slapstick or suggestive humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crude Humor
rubrics_metrics.description: Content includes humor that may seem vulgar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diverse Content: Discretion Advised
rubrics_metrics.description: Contains content with varying levels of maturity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A more general descriptor to signal mixed-maturity content elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drug Reference
rubrics_metrics.description: References to illegal drugs in any form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fantasy Violence
rubrics_metrics.description: Violent actions that look unrealistic and can easily be distinguished from reality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gambling Themes
rubrics_metrics.description: Prominently features images or activities typically associated with real-world gambling, even if not directly simulating a gambling experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intense Violence
rubrics_metrics.description: Graphic and realistic depictions of violence. May include weapons, human injury, blood, gore and/or death.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language
rubrics_metrics.description: Mild to moderate use of profanity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lyrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Mildly objectionable lyrics in the game's soundtrack containing profanities and/or references to sexuality, alcohol, tobacco, and/or drug use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mature Humor
rubrics_metrics.description: Content includes 'adult' humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nudity
rubrics_metrics.description: Depictions of nudity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial Nudity
rubrics_metrics.description: Brief and/or mild depictions of nudity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Real Gambling
rubrics_metrics.description: Player can gamble with real-life currency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sexual Content
rubrics_metrics.description: Depictions of sexual behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sexual Themes
rubrics_metrics.description: References to sex and/or sexuality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sexual Violence
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes violent, sexual acts including rape.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simulated Gambling
rubrics_metrics.description: Contains gameplay that simulates gambling activities without using real-life currency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong Language
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit/frequent use of profanity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong Lyrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Lyrics in the soundtrack contain explicit/frequent profanity and/or references to sexuality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong Sexual Content
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit and/or frequent sexual behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggestive Themes
rubrics_metrics.description: Mild references to sex and/or sexuality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tobacco Reference
rubrics_metrics.description: References to tobacco products in any form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Drugs
rubrics_metrics.description: Depictions of the use of real illegal drugs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Alcohol
rubrics_metrics.description: Depictions of alcohol consumption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Tobacco
rubrics_metrics.description: Depictions of the use of tobacco products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violent References
rubrics_metrics.description: References to violent acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violence
rubrics_metrics.description: Content includes aggressive behavior against an individual, community, self, or other real or fictional animals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interactive elements (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: An ESRB ratings label may include a section related to 'Interactive Elements' which discloses if a game offers online communications, collects personal data, or offers digital goods requiring real money.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These labels inform parents about features like online communications and in-game purchases without altering the age-rating categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: In-Game Purchases
rubrics_metrics.description: Game contains means to purchase in-game items with real-world money.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates presence of real-money transactions; introduced to inform consumers about monetization.

rubrics_metrics.name: In-Game Purchases (Includes Random Items)
rubrics_metrics.description: Game contains in-game offers to purchase digital goods or premiums with real world currency for which the player does not know prior to purchase the specific digital goods or premiums they will receive (loot boxes, item packs, mystery awards).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Labels loot-box type mechanics and randomized purchases; added as a separate interactive element.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shares Info
rubrics_metrics.description: Personal information such as email address, phone number or credit card is provided to third parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warns that personal data may be shared with third parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shares Location
rubrics_metrics.description: Can display the player's location with other players.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates potential privacy/location-sharing features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unrestricted Internet
rubrics_metrics.description: Product provides access to the internet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warns that the product gives users open internet access which may expose them to unmoderated content or communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Users Interact
rubrics_metrics.description: Players can get in direct communication with others through social media and networks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signals real-time or direct player-to-player communication capabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online Music Not Rated by the ESRB
rubrics_metrics.description: Warns that songs streamed or downloaded as add-ons for music-based games have not been rated and that their content was not considered in the ESRB rating assignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alerts consumers that additional unreviewed content may be present via streamed/downloaded music.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long Form (full rating submission) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A publisher submits a detailed questionnaire ('Long Form') describing graphic/extreme content and supplies a video demonstrating the content (gameplay footage/cutscenes). Information should include context, storyline, gameplay mechanics, reward systems, unlockable/hidden content, scripts and lyrics if provided, and payment of an upfront fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ESRB seeks enough contextual information to judge appropriateness; omissions may trigger inquiries, warnings, fines, or re-evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short Form / Questionnaire-based (digital/mobile) process
rubrics_metrics.description: A streamlined, automated Short Form (and later IARC questionnaire) requires publishers to answer multiple-choice questions about content categories (violence, sexual content, language, etc.) and automatically determines the rating category and content descriptors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used for digitally-distributed/mobile titles to scale ratings; games may be tested post-release to verify disclosed content. ESRB phased Short Form into IARC for many digital storefronts; retail physical releases must use Long Form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rater panel composition and review procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Material is sent to at least three different anonymous raters representing various demographics (including parents and casual/hardcore gamers); one lead rater writes the report, raters discuss appropriate rating and perform a parity analysis against similar past games.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most internal reviews take ~45 minutes; complex reviews may take up to four hours over multiple days; overall process ~one week. Raters are prevented from speaking directly with publishers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parity analysis and lead rater report
rubrics_metrics.description: The lead rater writes the report and works with staff to perform a parity analysis to ensure the assigned rating aligns with ratings from similar games in the past.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to maintain consistency across titles and avoid anomalous ratings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Omissions, clarification, warnings, and fines
rubrics_metrics.description: If inconsistencies or omissions are found between the Long Form and video footage, ESRB contacts the publisher for clarification; publishers receive warnings for omissions and may be fined for repeated infractions. Penalties for misrepresenting content include fines up to US$1 million and possible product recall to reprint labels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps ensure publishers disclose hidden/locked content and maintain accurate submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals process
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishers may question or appeal a rating; they can revise the game and resubmit for a new rating. ESRB has an appeals procedure, though as of 2007 it had never been used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ESRB does not instruct what must be changed to alter a rating, only which content triggered elements; publishers choose how to resolve.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-release monitoring, play testing and re-evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: When the final game is sent for release, ESRB reviews packaging and randomly play tests copies for thorough review (typically up to four hours). With post-release content patches, DLC, season passes and live-service updates, ESRB flags games and periodically checks new content to ensure it remains within the established rating; if not, re-evaluation is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ratings information is typically posted online ~30 days after completion; publishers may embargo ratings until official announcement to prevent leaks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embargo option for ratings information
rubrics_metrics.description: ESRB began to allow publishers to place embargoes on the release of rating information until a game is officially announced to prevent inadvertent leaks about unannounced titles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used when public posting of a new rating would prematurely reveal a game's existence or details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marketing and advertising guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: ESRB enforces guidelines to ensure packaging and promotional materials properly display the ESRB rating, marketing is tailored to target audiences (especially TV spots), restricts where promotional materials for Teen+ or higher can appear, prohibits glamorizing/exploiting a game's rating, and requires online marketing for 'Mature' or higher to be restricted to appropriately aged users.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board will work with publishers to correct objectionable marketing; forbids other organizations' ratings being shown alongside ESRB on publisher sites or social media.

rubrics_metrics.name: ESRB Website Council Code of Conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: A group of online gaming publications under the Website Council operate under a code requiring them to display ESRB ratings information for games they cover and implement systems to restrict access to audiovisual content of M or AO-rated games to users who are appropriately aged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Self-regulatory mechanism for web publishers to support age-appropriate access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retail and console enforcement (self-regulatory leverage)
rubrics_metrics.description: ESRB ratings are enforced primarily via voluntary industry leverage: most stores require photo ID for highest age ratings and refuse to stock unrated or AO titles; major console manufacturers will not license games for their systems unless they carry ESRB ratings (and often refuse AO titles).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This voluntary enforcement is a key compliance mechanism; some jurisdictions also enforce ESRB via film/ratings boards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parental controls and storefront filtering
rubrics_metrics.description: Modern consoles include parental controls that can restrict games by ESRB rating; online storefronts can filter and restrict titles based on ESRB/IARC-generated ratings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used by parents and retailers to limit access for younger users.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy certification / 'Privacy Certified' program
rubrics_metrics.description: ESRB offers an online privacy program to help websites and mobile apps adopt privacy policies and data practices that comply with laws and best practices, providing 'Privacy Certified' seals indicating certification under ESRB privacy guidelines (extended to mobile apps partly to help with COPPA compliance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A separate certification service, distinct from content ratings, focused on data usage and privacy practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short Form disallowed for retail physical releases; value tier for low-budget titles
rubrics_metrics.description: In ~2017 ESRB instituted rules mandating that any retail product undergo the standard Long Form review (disallowing Short Form for retail), and introduced a 'value tier' pricing for Long Form reviews for games developed at lower budgets (under $1 million) with a $3000 fee for retail rating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affected indie publishers and retail release decisions; intended to ensure retail-quality review rigor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Label/icon design and display clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: ESRB rating icons and label appearance have been updated to increase clarity at smaller sizes (e.g., on mobile): textual name black on white, removal of 'content rated by' tagline, repositioning of trademark symbols, and full labels typically displayed on the back of packaging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Icon design changes aim to improve legibility across physical and digital storefronts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Associated media review for marketing materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Besides evaluating games, ESRB reviews marketing and advertising materials for games that have undergone rating to ensure they include the rating and that marketing is appropriate for the target audience; ESRB will request corrections for objectionable marketing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes guidance on what content is reasonable for certain game types and forbids inappropriate gratuitous presentation in ads/trailers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Green-band trailer clearing and limited relaxation for M-rated promos
rubrics_metrics.description: In March 2013 ESRB allowed (case-by-case) trailers for games that are or anticipated to be 'Mature' to be cleared as appropriate for 'general' audiences—similar to MPAA green-band—but with case-by-case conditions; also allowed limited cross-promotion of M-rated games in materials for lower-rated games depending on target demographics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Represents conditional loosening of prior marketing restrictions for mature titles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Steam/Epic/digital storefront policies interaction
rubrics_metrics.description: Digital storefronts vary in how they treat ESRB ratings: Steam displays ratings when available but does not require ESRB; Epic Games Store prohibits AO-rated games unless AO solely for blockchain use; platforms may ban content that violates payment processors' rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ESRB ratings do not override platform-specific content policies; developers must account for storefront rules in addition to ESRB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement that downloadable/post-release content remain consistent with original rating
rubrics_metrics.description: Games that provide post-release downloadable content must ensure new content remains consistent with the original ESRB rating; otherwise the ESRB requires the original game be re-evaluated and remarked with the more appropriate rating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Live-service updates, DLC and patches may trigger re-rating if they introduce content outside original scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement penalties and remedies for misuse of rating icons
rubrics_metrics.description: ESRB takes action against distributors who use rating icons without authorization or without having been issued the rating. Penalties for misrepresenting content can include fines up to US$1 million and product recalls to reprint labels if necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects integrity of the rating mark and deters false advertising.
